The patient has a 12-year history of recurrent follicular lymphoma, which is a type of non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
The patient presented with a subacute, multifocal, pruritic, and painful eruption, which is consistent with a drug-induced skin reaction, given his recent medication changes.
The patient's skin lesions, including well-demarcated erythematous plaques and scaly papules, are consistent with psoriasis, although the diagnosis of a psoriasiform drug reaction takes precedence.

The patient's history of follicular lymphoma and the presence of skin lesions raise the possibility of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma, although the findings are more consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction.

The patient's history of follicular lymphoma and the presence of skin lesions raise the possibility of paraneoplastic pemphigus, although the findings are more consistent with a psoriasiform drug reaction.
